scope: Isolated response-worker, deferred reconstruction and incremental hash experiment; not a production fix
method: Move artifact_read result serialization and HTTP delivery to a disposable worker, retaining the previous experimental decoder changes. With the original PLY-3, run GUI Split and Extract, export, read the entire artifact through public MCP with chunk-length checks and an incremental download hash, delete the artifact, then open an existing project in the GUI without forced garbage collection and compare core geometry digests.
result: The 475566423-byte read completed and the GUI opened the project; source, cutter and extracted-part core digests matched and the page reported no errors. The download SHA-256 was 4e8928bed8f15d80dca88767d58472eb52b93f38222266d331ec59aee5df431f; it was not independently compared with an authoritative exported-file hash. The guard reported success and cleanup, but its peak of 4299132928 bytes exceeded the nominal 4294967296-byte limit, so the resource gate does not pass.

responseWorkerOnlyControl.method: The same response-worker prototype and real download with chunk-length checks, but the unmodified 94153b76 project decoder. Run without the extra process profiler and without forced garbage collection.
responseWorkerOnlyControl.result: The 475566423-byte download completed, then GUI reopen and its page-state probe timed out. Peak job bytes 4537548800 exceeded the nominal limit; cleanup was confirmed. The downloaded SHA-256 aa440bd2ab92c8c2d52c3a820b5beeca67485aff9327aaa22b7a540152c24071 has no independent export reference.

downloadedFileReopen.method: Using the combined experimental build, write every actual MCP artifact chunk to an owned local file while hashing it, then open that downloaded file in the GUI without forced collection or process-profile snapshots.
downloadedFileReopen.result: The 475566423-byte downloaded file had SHA-256 77aabaeac8cc2b1b1663f772fb3161d3d3989f4596dfc3c6f00d29537ba970d1, independently verified on disk. The decoder returned its packet after validating the project chunks, but GUI open and the page probe timed out. Peak job bytes 4313767936 exceeded the 4294967296 limit; remaining descendants were terminated and cleanup confirmed. No post-reopen geometry was obtained.

mainReconstructionTrace.method: Repeat the actual downloaded-file reopen with diagnostic events around main-thread numeric-buffer reuse and allocation; no forced collection or process-profile snapshots.
mainReconstructionTrace.result: The decoder returned four numeric buffers. The first, containing 33263505 values, matched and reused an existing array and reached ready. The next buffer contained 5612016 values; its reuse check started but no match or allocation event appeared before the GUI and page probe timed out. Peak job bytes 4314853376 exceeded the nominal limit; cleanup was confirmed. This is the last reported stage, not proof of an exact allocation or scheduling cause.

reuseYieldAndBase64Diagnostics.method: Instrument the second array's cooperative reuse comparison. The first run uses the existing base64 conversion; the second uses native Uint8Array.toBase64 with the original conversion as fallback in the combined experimental build. Both use the real downloaded file and no forced collection.
reuseYieldAndBase64Diagnostics.yieldTrace: Build scanforge-aeb73f968795d07f timed out before the decoder returned, so the new reuse events were not reached. Peak job bytes 4324261888 exceeded the nominal limit; cleanup confirmed. Log SHA-256 104ae88ab49fbd1197147abf752551f13652f934a73a1a57d95664c767a50dd4; guard SHA-256 54f35cf73bf32456e54d42a311a94a5da762b9084c8a531ccd5d4e92aeb362a4.
reuseYieldAndBase64Diagnostics.nativeBase64: Build scanforge-2684aee0e4a5ebab downloaded and reopened the 475566423-byte file, matched source, cutter and extracted geometry digests, and reported no page errors. All four numeric arrays reused existing arrays; the second comparison and its observed yields completed. Peak job bytes 4295688192 exceeded the 4294967296-byte limit by 720896 bytes, so this is not resource acceptance despite the guard's success status. Cleanup confirmed. The download hash 2e5cac8f284f04de396cdb2b63880053d2e8e9aea1b4b419a68749d56bf03680 has no independent reference.
reuseYieldAndBase64Diagnostics.browserControl: Installed headless Chrome 156 native conversion matched the existing btoa path for nine deterministic lengths from 0 to 1048576 bytes, including 262144. Browser control guard SHA-256 02c7b3bdd795c8d500859f37962b5371c95e17d829b8790ba39a87110b66a87b.
reuseYieldAndBase64Diagnostics.limits: Separate single runs cannot prove the base64 change caused the difference. The worker, deferred decoder, hash, conversion and tracing are unreviewed experimental changes; the strict resource gate, independent transfer integrity, public-MCP reopen and native acceptance remain open.

limits: Single instrumented run with three experimental changes; their individual effects are not established. The worker lacks production lifecycle, cancellation, error, authorization and compatibility review. No independent full-download integrity, public-MCP import after download, post-reopen history, full suite, native Split acceptance or resource guarantee is established. No application change was integrated.
